Clipora and Ditto: two ways to keep your copies.

Ditto is an established open-source Windows clipboard manager. Both apps can keep local history and retrieve older copies; the useful distinction is how each fits your routine.

Reviewed 29 October 2026 · Clipora editorial

The documented workflows

Choose by the work you need to do
Your taskDitto 3.25.113.0Clipora
Find a previous copyLocal database; description/full-text, wildcard and regex search options in stable source.Encrypted local history with token-prefix search, collections and tags.
Keep and order favoritesSticky positioning and Never Auto Delete are separate options.Pins appear first and are protected from automatic retention; explicit confirmed deletion can remove them.
Paste without formattingShift + Enter and special-paste transformations are documented in stable source.Alt + Enter or the clip’s plain-paste action; typing and copy-only options are also available.
Reuse text and automateGroups, shortcuts and ChaiScript copy/paste processing.Placeholder snippets, transformations, triggers and trusted C#/VB.NET macros. Trusted macros are not sandboxed.
Back up or transferDatabase backup/restore, clip import/export and configurable computer/IP transfer.Password-encrypted backup/merge restore; optional encrypted folder/private-server sync.
Use it locallyOfficial site advertises no login, cloud or telemetry; configurable network features still exist.No app account or app analytics; local by default, optional sync starts off.

Documentation comparison, checked 29 October 2026. Clipora baseline: Store package 2.0.5.0 x64. These are documented workflows, not head-to-head speed, reliability or security benchmarks. “Not verified” does not mean unavailable.

Choose the details you will use

Consider Ditto if an open-source clipboard manager, advanced search options and its existing special-paste or scripting workflows fit you. Its public source and portable distribution can matter as much as appearance.

Consider Clipora if you prefer its compact picker, pin-first organization, native workspace, placeholder snippets and password-encrypted portable backup workflow. Its image actions include offline Windows OCR; this review does not establish whether Ditto offers an equivalent built-in OCR workflow.

Local does not mean identical

Both products support local use. That is not a unique selling point for either. Their database, backup, network and script behavior differ; review the settings before copying sensitive information.

Clipora’s history encryption has explicit limits, and its trusted macros run as full .NET code. Read the privacy notice before enabling optional features.

Use your destination apps as the deciding test

With synthetic content, retrieve a text clip, paste an image into a compatible document and test plain paste into your regular editor. Check keyboard access and the window sizes you use. Back up a small test library and verify its restore before trusting any backup routine.

We have not run a controlled head-to-head benchmark or restored a Ditto database for this article. No relative speed, security or paste-reliability score is claimed.
